title: `TIME` is off by default; with it on, `TIME + INTERVAL` raises past midnight
verdict: `time_interval_months`: `TIME` unsupported by default; `+ INTERVAL 1 MONTH` a type error
description: Spark 4.3.0 parses `TIME` only with `spark.sql.timeType.enabled` on; by default `TIME'12:00:00'` raises `UNSUPPORTED_TIME_TYPE`. With it on, `TIME'12:00:00' + INTERVAL 13 HOUR` raises `DATETIME_OVERFLOW` rather than wrapping past midnight, in both modes, and `TIME + INTERVAL 1 MONTH` is rejected when the query is analysed (`DATATYPE_MISMATCH.BINARY_OP_DIFF_TYPES`).
reference: `TIME ± INTERVAL` is refused (`time_interval_months`). Spark refuses `TIME` by default too.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `'10:00:01' :: TIME(1) - INTERVAL '1' MONTH` fails analysis with `DATATYPE_MISMATCH.BINARY_OP_DIFF_TYPES`, ANSI on (the suite enables `TIME` under tests)
`TIME(4) + INTERVAL '01:04:05.56' HOUR TO SECOND` is a `time(6)`, `13:47:38.6834`

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
